help.markdown:
> shadow-utils (aka shadow) 4.4 through 4.17.0 establishes a default /etc/subuid behavior (e.g., uid 100000 through 165535 for the first user account) that can realistically conflict with the uids of users defined on locally administered networks, potentially leading to account takeover, e.g., by leveraging newuidmap for access to an NFS home directory (or same-host resources in the case of remote logins by these local network users). NOTE: it may also be argued that system administrators should not have assigned uids, within local networks, that are within the range that can occur in /etc/subuid.

|                                                                                                                   |
|Package         pkg:deb/ubuntu/shadow@1%3A4.13%2Bdfsg1-4ubuntu3.2?os_distro=noble&os_name=ubuntu&os_version=24.04  |
|Affected range  >=0                                                                                                |
|Fixed version   not fixed                                                                                          |

> Passing an effectively empty string to the `,ccs=` syntax extension of the mode argument in the `fopen` function in the GNU C Library version 2.45 or earlier may result in a heap buffer overflow when the mode string input to the function is attacker controlled.    This usage pattern is not seen in applications in common GNU/Linux distributions and applications that process user-supplied values for `ccs` should not pass them through without validation.

|Package         pkg:deb/ubuntu/glibc@2.39-0ubuntu8.9?os_distro=noble&os_name=ubuntu&os_version=24.04  |

help.markdown:
> A flaw was found in libdm. A local attacker could craft a malicious Logical Volume Manager (LVM) metadata configuration with deeply nested structures. This could lead to uncontrolled recursion in the libdm configuration file parser, exhausting the stack and causing any LVM command reading the metadata to crash. This vulnerability results in a Denial of Service (DoS) for affected systems.

|                                                                                                        |
|Package         pkg:deb/ubuntu/lvm2@2.03.16-3ubuntu3.2?os_distro=noble&os_name=ubuntu&os_version=24.04  |
|Affected range  >=0                                                                                     |
|Fixed version   not fixed                                                                               |
help.text: A flaw was found in libdm. A local attacker could craft a malicious Logical Volume Manager (LVM) metadata configuration with deeply nested structures. This could lead to uncontrolled recursion in the libdm configuration file parser, exhausting the stack and causing any LVM command reading the metadata to crash. This vulnerability results in a Denial of Service (DoS) for affected systems.

help.markdown:
> zlib versions 1.3.1.2 through 1.3.2 contain a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the gz_vacate() function when processing non-blocking gzwrite() operations with stale external buffer pointers. Attackers can trigger the overflow by calling gzprintf() or gzvprintf() after a write stall, causing an unchecked memmove() to write beyond the internal input buffer boundary.

|                                                                                                               |
|Package         pkg:deb/ubuntu/zlib@1%3A1.3.dfsg-3.1ubuntu2.2?os_distro=noble&os_name=ubuntu&os_version=24.04  |
|Affected range  >=0                                                                                            |
|Fixed version   not fixed                                                                                      |
help.text: zlib versions 1.3.1.2 through 1.3.2 contain a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the gz_vacate() function when processing non-blocking gzwrite() operations with stale external buffer pointers. Attackers can trigger the overflow by calling gzprintf() or gzvprintf() after a write stall, causing an unchecked memmove() to write beyond the internal input buffer boundary.

RIAK_GID: Optional nonzero GID for riak; empty retains the package GID. Mounted directories are chowned.
RIAK_LOG_MAX_FILES: Maximum file count per OpenRiak logger handler; initializes new configurations only.
RIAK_LOG_MAX_FILE_SIZE: Maximum size per OpenRiak logger file; initializes new configurations only.
RIAK_UID: Optional nonzero UID for riak; empty retains the package UID. Mounted directories are chowned.
TZ: IANA timezone for the process and entrypoint logs, for example Asia/Tokyo.

setting_comments.OPENRIAK_CLUSTER_CONTROL_DIR: Container directory shared by cluster discovery participants.
setting_comments.OPENRIAK_CLUSTER_CONTROL_PATH: Host directory shared by all cluster discovery participants.
setting_comments.OPENRIAK_CLUSTER_MODE: Use single-node startup or shared-directory cluster discovery.
setting_comments.OPENRIAK_CLUSTER_WAIT_SECONDS: Maximum seconds to wait for cluster discovery approval.
setting_comments.OPENRIAK_CPUS: CPU limit per node, for example 2.0; 0 means unrestricted.
setting_comments.OPENRIAK_DOCKER_LOG_MAX_FILES: Maximum number of Docker JSON log files retained per node.
setting_comments.OPENRIAK_DOCKER_LOG_MAX_SIZE: Maximum size of each Docker JSON log file per node.
setting_comments.OPENRIAK_HTTP_PORT: Host port forwarded to container HTTP port 8098.
setting_comments.OPENRIAK_MEMORY_LIMIT: Memory limit per node, for example 4g; 0 means unrestricted.
setting_comments.OPENRIAK_PB_PORT: Host port forwarded to container Protocol Buffers port 8087.
setting_comments.RIAK_ANTI_ENTROPY: Legacy active anti-entropy mode (passive disables active exchanges).
setting_comments.RIAK_DISTRIBUTED_COOKIE: Initial cookie; existing riak.conf wins and new followers adopt the coordinator cookie.
setting_comments.RIAK_GID: Optional nonzero GID for riak; empty retains the package GID. Mounted directories are chowned.
setting_comments.RIAK_HTTP_LISTENER: Container HTTP bind address and port.
setting_comments.RIAK_INIT_ONLY: Initialize configuration and directories without starting the daemon when 1.
setting_comments.RIAK_LOG_MAX_FILES: Maximum file count per OpenRiak logger handler; initializes new configurations only.
setting_comments.RIAK_LOG_MAX_FILE_SIZE: Maximum size per OpenRiak logger file; initializes new configurations only.
setting_comments.RIAK_NODE_HOST: DNS hostname used to derive the OpenRiak KV nodename.
setting_comments.RIAK_NOFILE_LIMIT: Requested open-file limit; bounded by container ulimits.
setting_comments.RIAK_PB_LISTENER: Container Protocol Buffers bind address and port.
setting_comments.RIAK_RING_SIZE: Partition count for a new ring; do not change on an existing cluster.
setting_comments.RIAK_STORAGE_BACKEND: Storage backend used by OpenRiak KV.
setting_comments.RIAK_TICTACAAE_STOREHEADS: Store object heads in the TicTac anti-entropy store.
setting_comments.RIAK_UID: Optional nonzero UID for riak; empty retains the package UID. Mounted directories are chowned.
setting_comments.TZ: IANA timezone for the process and entrypoint logs, for example Asia/Tokyo.
setting_comments.role: Coordinator on exactly one cluster service; empty or omitted means follower.

history.created_by: LABEL org.opencontainers.image.description=Package-backed OpenRiak KV with single-node and cluster startup support

RUN /bin/sh -c set -eu
if ! getent group riak >/dev/null 2>&1
then
    groupadd --system riak
fi
if ! id riak >/dev/null 2>&1
then
    useradd --system --gid riak --home-dir /var/lib/riak --shell /sbin/nologin riak
fi
test -x /usr/sbin/riak
id riak
mkdir -p /opt/openriak-defaults/etc-riak /var/lib/riak /var/log/riak /run/riak /usr/lib/riak/log
cp -a /etc/riak/. /opt/openriak-defaults/etc-riak/
chown -R riak:riak /var/lib/riak /var/log/riak /run/riak /usr/lib/riak/log
 # buildkit
